sentences.text: Learned counsel for the Petitioners argues  that the accident occurred sole due to the rash and  negligent driving of the offending vehicle the accident  occurred and thereby petitioners sustained grievous  injuries.

Whereas learned Counsel for the Respondent  no 2 has vehemently argued, both orally and by way  of written submissions, that the petitioner has failed to  SCCH.13 10 MVC.4886 & 4887/2023  establish the claim as pleaded.

It is contended that  there are significant inconsistencies between the  pleadings and the evidence on record, and therefore,
 the petitioners are not entitled to any relief.

The  counsel further submitted that the Tribunal must  independently assess the involvement and negligence  of the alleged offending vehicle without solely relying  upon judgments or documents emanating from the  criminal proceedings.

19. It was argued that mere filing of charge sheet  by the police or production of police documents by the  petitioner cannot be accepted as conclusive proof of  negligence or involvement of the vehicle.

According to  the respondent no 1, absence of a challenge by the  accused driver to the police findings or a lack of  objection should not automatically bind third parties  such as insurers, who may suffer prejudice from such  assumptions.

In support of this contention, reliance  was placed on judicial pronouncements including  2007 ACJ 1928 (SC), between Oriental Insurance  Co Ltd. V Premalatha Shulka and others, Civil  Appeal No. 8352 of 2019, and Criminal Appeal No.

It is a settled legal principle that  when official documents such as FIR and charge sheet,
 are consistent and un rebutted, they carry evidentiary  value.
 22.

In the present case, the respondent no 2  failed to confront PW1 or PW2 with any challenge  regarding the occurrence of the accident or the alleged  SCCH.13 12 MVC.4886 & 4887/2023  involvement of the offending vehicle, except for raising  questions on the nature of injuries sustained.
23 . As is evident from the records, the accident  occurred on 9.4.2023, and the complaint was lodged  on 10.4.2023.
The brother of petitioner in  MVC.4886/2023 filed complaint narrating the manner  of the accident and specifically mentioning the  involvement of the offending vehicle.
The explanation  provided by the complainant for the delay in lodging  the complaint is that the petitioners were undergoing  medical treatment.

The medical records marked as  Ex.P7 and EXP14 support this explanation and show  that the petitioners were taken to the Hosmat  hospital, Bengaluru, this sequence of events explains  the delay in lodging the complaint.
 24.
After due investigation, the police filed a  charge sheet against the driver of the offending  vehicle.
While according to the respondent no 1  claimed that the offending vehicle was not involved in  the accident and that the injuries sustained by the  petitioner were not caused by the said vehicle
, neither  the driver nor the owner of the vehicle chose to  SCCH.13 13 MVC.4886 & 4887/2023  challenge the charge sheet or resist the final report  before the appropriate court.

25 . Furthermore, respondent no 1 in an attempt  to counter the direct testimony of the petitioner and  the corroborating entries in the medical records and  investigation report, has offered nothing during the  cross-examination of PW1 and PW2.
No cogent  evidence has been produced to disprove the  petitioners' version of events.

In the absence of any  credible and substantive evidence to the contrary, this  tribunal finds no merit in the assertion made by  respondent no 2 that the vehicle was not involved in  the accident and that there is no connection between  the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the  accident involving the said vehicle.

No specific documents were produced by  PW3 to corroborate certain elements of his oral  testimony; however, his findings were consistent with  the clinical records and scan reports produced on  record.
34. Though the petitioner was treated  conservatively, the injury sustained was in close  proximity to the hip joint , resulting in restricted  mobility of that joint.
It is well established that the hip  joint plays a crucial role in mobility, balance and the  performance of routine daily activities.

Any impairment  SCCH.13 17 MVC.4886 & 4887/2023  to this joint not only affects the petitioner's personal  life but also has a significant bearing on his ability to  carry our his vocational responsibilities, especially  considering the nature of his work.
